description:
GH: https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam/issues/21

`bn status` printed:

    warnings:
      clock_skew: 3657601 ms ahead (at 2026-08-12 04:07)

~61 minutes. Then ~20 min later, with NO corrective action — no clock change, no
daemon restart, nothing — the warning just disappeared.

Reporter is NOT claiming the detection is wrong (their host had
`System clock synchronized: no`, NTP inactive). The complaint is the message is
not actionable: cannot tell a `bn` bug from a host clock problem without guessing.

What the message must say:
  1. WHICH TWO CLOCKS. "ahead" of what? Local system clock vs a store timestamp?
     vs another actor's clock in the store? vs the git remote? Right now names
     neither side.
  2. DIRECTION, unambiguously. "3657601 ms ahead" doesn't say whether local is
     ahead of the reference or the reference is ahead of local. Opposite fixes.
  3. WHAT IT AFFECTS. Does skew this size threaten issue ordering, dedup, or
     last-write-wins? Or purely informational?
  4. WHY IT CAN CLEAR ITSELF. Appears and vanishes with no user action = reads
     like a measurement artefact. If it IS transient (stale timestamp aging out
     of the comparison window), say so, so nobody chases a clock problem that
     isn't there.

Reporter's suggested shape:
    clock_skew: local system clock is 61m 0s behind actor <id>'s last write
    (2026-08-12 04:07); may affect ordering

Also worth a doc line on the self-clearing window, wherever the warning is
computed.
title: kopi-beans: clock_skew warning doesn't name which two clocks it compared, and self-clears
